strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across two task types, multiple model families, and extensive ablations including transferability to larger models, compositionality, memory efficiency, and VLM extension

Clear practical benefits demonstrated: enables model-agnostic reasoning guidance without retraining frozen backbones, achieves 2x higher batch sizes than LoRA, and enables composable task-specific modules
Well-executed presentation with effective visualizations and concrete qualitative examples showing clear synergy between backbone and reasoning module components
Addresses a real problem (expensive LLM fine-tuning, poor LoRA transferability) with an elegant decomposition approach to translate trajectory-level rewards into token-level guidance
Detailed reproducibility support: comprehensive hyperparameters, prompt templates, example outputs, and promise of code release
weaknesses: Core technical assumption (Eq. 4) that trajectory rewards decompose as sum of token log-probabilities lacks empirical validation; no analysis of approximation error or robustness when assumption is violated

Theorem 1 provides only weak theoretical justification with circular reasoning (assumes Eq. 4 to prove it), lacks rigor on convergence guarantees, and doesn't justify why training for rewards yields the assumed decomposition

Critical infrastructure limitation underexplored: inference requires two forward passes (backbone + reasoning module), doubling latency compared to baseline; paper acknowledges but minimizes this practical constraint without wall-clock measurements

Mixed empirical results contradict main claims: Qwen2.5-3B results show UniR (82.2) underperforms GRPO Full (82.8) on GSM8K; out-of-distribution improvements marginal (AIME24: 10.0% vs 13.3-16.7% for baselines)

Method applicability severely limited to tasks with predefined/verifiable rewards (rule-based correctness, BLEU scores); cannot handle preference-based signals, human feedback, or open-ended generation tasks

Key design choice of removing KL regularization (βKL=0) lacks rigorous justification beyond vague appeal to 'exploration freedom'; no ablation study and minimal reference to related work (DAPO) without deep engagement
Incomplete analysis of compositionality: optimal mixing weights (α in Eq. 6) require task-specific tuning, no principled method for N modules, scalability untested beyond 2 modules

Limited baseline comparisons: GenARM mentioned but not compared experimentally; no comparison with learned composition weights vs. fixed logit addition; GRPO baselines use untuned Hugging Face defaults
Sparse ablation studies missing sensitivity analysis on temperature β, impact of reward formulation choices, reasoning module architecture beyond size, and isolated effects of design modifications

Reward decomposition justification relies on single citation [40] discussing abstract equivalence classes without demonstrating decomposability for specific reward functions (exact match vs. continuous metrics like BLEU)

strengths: Addresses practical challenges with full fine-tuning (cost) and LoRA (transferability, composition) through a clean modular logit-addition approach
Comprehensive experimental setup with multiple models, datasets, and detailed hyperparameter specifications in appendix enabling reproducibility attempts
Demonstrates clear memory efficiency gains: supports batch size 128 vs 64/32 for LoRA/full tuning under 80GB, with detailed VRAM analysis
Shows evidence of transferability: 0.5B reasoning module trained with 3B backbone improves 8B/14B models without fine-tuning
Provides composability demonstration combining math and translation modules for bilingual tasks
Well-motivated problem addressing real limitations of existing methods
weaknesses: Core theoretical assumption in Eq. (4) lacks justification—no evidence provided that trajectory-level rewards decompose into summed token-level log-probabilities from GRPO-trained πr. Theorem 1 is circular, assuming this decomposition rather than proving it.

Experimental results are inconsistent and selectively presented: UniR underperforms GRPO Full on Qwen (42.2 vs 44.8) and translation tasks (67.87 vs 72.14), contradicting claims of 'significant outperformance' over 'baseline fine-tuning methods'
Inference-time computational cost is substantial (two forward passes) but largely ignored. No wall-clock inference time comparisons provided despite training efficiency being a key motivation.
Transferability gains are modest: 3.2% on 14B, 5.4% on 8B. Questions whether πr captures generalizable reasoning or is task/model-specific despite 'Universal' framing.
Limited applicability: approach only works for tasks with predefined, verifiable rewards (math, BLEU scores). No evaluation on open-ended reasoning tasks, contradicting 'Universal' claims.
Weak composability evidence: single task demonstrated with obvious α-based trade-offs. No comparison to direct fine-tuning on composite tasks. Logit addition is trivial; non-obvious benefits unclear.
Ad-hoc design choices lack principled justification: setting βKL=0 based on vague argument about πr initialization; max_steps, learning rates chosen without sensitivity analysis.

Figure 3 contradicts motivation: standalone πr produces 'repetitive and logically flawed reasoning,' yet paper claims its logits meaningfully guide backbone. Mechanism for why poor logits help unclear.
Statistical rigor absent: no error bars, significance testing, or reporting of standard deviations across multiple runs. Claimed improvements may not be statistically significant.
Reproducibility compromised: abstract states 'code is open-sourced at [MISSING]'—no repository link provided. Some hyperparameter choices unjustified despite reproducibility claims.

strengths: Novel decomposition framework: Elegant approach of separating reasoning into a lightweight, independently trained module that can be combined with any frozen backbone through logit addition
Practical efficiency gains: Demonstrated 2-4x increase in batch size compared to LoRA and full fine-tuning; reduced memory for intermediate activations
Transferability across model sizes: A reasoning module trained on 3B backbone effectively guides 14B models without retraining, enabling weak-to-strong generalization
Composability through module addition: Multiple specialized reasoning modules can be combined via logit addition (Eq. 6) without additional training, enabling modular multi-objective reasoning

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple tasks (math reasoning, translation, composition, VLMs), multiple model families (Llama, Qwen), both in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks, with detailed ablations and qualitative analysis
Clear presentation and reproducibility: Well-structured paper with intuitive figures, detailed hyperparameters, prompt templates, and code promise
Honest reporting of limitations: Acknowledges cases where method doesn't outperform GRPO Full (Qwen2.5) and discusses inherent limitations of frozen backbone approach
weaknesses: Inconsistent empirical improvements: UniR (42.2) does not surpass GRPO Full (44.8) for Qwen2.5-3B, undermining the 'superior performance' claim and suggesting gains may be model/task-dependent rather than universal

Weak empirical validation of core assumption (Eq. 4): The trajectory reward decomposition is theoretically motivated but not empirically validated; paper does not demonstrate that πᵣ actually learns to satisfy Σ log πᵣ(yₜ|...) = r(x,y), only that GRPO training works
Removal of KL regularization creates asymmetry: Setting βKL = 0 in UniR while baselines use β = 0.04 creates a confounding factor that complicates interpretation of performance differences

Limited scope and applicability: Method restricted to tasks with predefined, rule-based rewards (correctness, BLEU); cannot handle preference-based learning with human annotations, limiting real-world applicability
Incomplete theoretical justification: Theorem 1 is somewhat tautological—assumes πᵣ satisfies Eq. 4 to prove equivalence to Q*, but the assumption itself needs independent validation

Missing cross-family transfer analysis: All experiments train reasoning modules from models in the same family as backbones (Qwen with Qwen, Llama with Llama); cross-family transfer not tested, questioning 'architecture-agnostic' claims

Limited analysis of what reasoning module learns: While Figure 3 shows qualitative examples, there is insufficient investigation of learned representations or sensitivity analysis on design choices (e.g., impact of βKL = 0)
Incomplete experimental reporting: No error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance testing; number of runs not specified; cross-family and cross-size scaling studies limited

strengths: Theoretically principled framework with sound mathematical justification (Theorem 4.1 connecting trained module to optimal Q-function); empirical validation supports core assumptions (Figure 5 reward decomposition)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 6+ diverse domains (math, translation, VLMs, medical) with proper statistical reporting (means and std devs over 10 seeds), relevant baselines, and thorough ablations

Demonstrates three valuable practical properties: modularity (preserves backbone), transferability (1.5B modules improve 8B/14B models), and composability (German math translation example convincingly shows multi-module coordination)
Strong robustness advantage over GRPO Full under stochastic decoding (minimal temperature sensitivity: 42.7% at T=0.6 vs 36.1% for GRPO Full; this addresses real deployment concerns)
Honest discussion of limitations in Appendix C; thorough engineering analysis (gradient stability, VRAM scaling, training dynamics) demonstrates rigor beyond empirical results
Clear potential for impact: modular approach addresses real pain point in adapting frozen LLMs; promised open-source code enhances reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited theoretical novelty: reward decomposition (Eq. 4) directly applies Xu et al. (2024b) Theorem 3; core contribution is the engineering combination rather than fundamental insight

Non-standard training setup (β_KL=0) deviates from GRPO without sufficient ablation justifying this choice; while justified via DAPO reference, this makes it unclear how much improvement comes from UniR vs avoiding standard regularization
Restricted applicability: limited to verifiable reward tasks (mathematical reasoning, translation, classification), cannot handle open-ended generation; this significantly constrains practical scope

Tokenizer dependence undermines 'universal' claims: cross-tokenizer transfer severely degraded (Table 10: 35.6→18.3 even with EVA alignment); method is only architecture-agnostic within same model family

AIME24 results are inconsistent and sometimes show no improvement (Qwen: 7.7±2.7 vs GRPO Full: 4.7±2.3 with high variance); suggests improvements may be sensitive to specific benchmarks rather than universally strong

Inference efficiency requires additional machinery: naive logit addition increases latency 57% (Table 6); claims of efficiency only hold with speculative decoding (CoS), adding implementation complexity not present in standard GRPO
Modest improvements under greedy decoding (Table 16: Qwen 43.9 vs GRPO Full 44.8); primary advantage is robustness to temperature rather than fundamentally superior reasoning

Composability analysis is underdeveloped: demonstrated only on artificial multi-task; 'negative interference' for conflicting modules mentioned but not analyzed; no principled method for selecting α weights
Medical domain validation limited to simple classification tasks (binary readmission, 4-class LOS prediction) on MIMIC-IV; scope narrower than suggested by healthcare motivation

Missing ablations: no study isolating impact of β_KL=0 choice; no comparison with parameter-level module fusion; incomplete failure case analysis (Figure 22) lacks guidance on when decomposition assumption breaks

strengths: Practical system design with genuine efficiency advantages (memory, modularity, architecture-agnosticism) and clean logit-level combination mechanism
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple domains (math, translation, medical, vision-language) with extensive ablations and reproducibility effort
Robust performance across sampling temperatures while GRPO baseline degrades significantly, providing practical value for deployed systems
Empirical validation of core assumptions (Figure 5) showing reasoning module learns reward alignment
Clear presentation with detailed implementation details, hyperparameters, and extensive appendices
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core contributions largely assemble existing pieces (reward decomposition from Xu et al. 2024b, logit-level guidance known from RAST/GenARM); fundamental innovation is modest

Unfair baseline comparisons: GRPO uses β_KL=0.04 while UniR uses β_KL=0 (different algorithm), making direct comparison invalid; GRPO's extreme temperature sensitivity (e.g., 42.4%→36.1% on MATH-500) appears suspicious and uninvestigated

Composability claims not convincingly demonstrated: single German-English example, medical composition shows combined modules underperform individual ones (Table 3), no principled weight selection, acknowledged negative interference not addressed

Weak-to-strong generalization overclaimed: logit addition to stronger model unsurprising; pre-trained 1.5B model also improves 14B baseline (43.7% vs 33.7%) without UniR fine-tuning, suggesting ensemble effects dominate over true knowledge transfer
Core assumption (Eq. 4) incompletely validated: Figure 5 shows correlation not proof; no analysis of when decomposition fails, reasoning module capacity limits, or out-of-distribution behavior
Inference cost underexplored: Table 12 shows UniR slower than LoRA (6.29 vs 4.67 sec/step); solution (CoS) is orthogonal technique; real hardware wall-clock time not reported

Experimental design concerns: non-standard temperature selection (T=0.6) complicates literature comparison; no statistical significance testing; large standard deviations make some improvements borderline
Limited medical domain validation: single dataset, mostly classification tasks, generalization to unseen mortality task lacks held-out test set validation

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear practical implications—addresses real limitations of LoRA (architectural constraints, poor ensemble properties) and full fine-tuning (computational cost)
Solid theoretical framework connecting trajectory rewards to token-level guidance, with proper mathematical justification for the reward decomposition through logit addition

Comprehensive experimental validation across diverse domains (mathematics, machine translation, medical reasoning, vision-language models) with proper statistical reporting (pass@1 with stochastic sampling over 10 seeds)
Demonstrates genuine transferability of reasoning modules across model scales (1.5B module trained with 3B backbone effectively enhances 8B and 14B models) without additional fine-tuning
Clear evidence of composability through weighted logit summation, enabling multi-task reasoning without architectural modification or retraining
Superior robustness to stochastic decoding compared to full fine-tuning—GRPO Full drops 4.5+ points at T=0.6 while UniR drops only ~1.2 points, critical for realistic deployment
Thorough computational efficiency analysis showing improved VRAM usage (batch 128 vs 64 for LoRA), stable gradient dynamics, and lower training variance
Excellent reproducibility with detailed hyperparameters, prompt templates, implementation details, and promised open-source code
Honest limitations discussion with empirical evidence of failure modes and acknowledgment of tokenizer constraints and bounded-by-backbone limitations
weaknesses: Limited theoretical novelty—the core reward decomposition result (Lemma A.1) is Theorem 3 from Xu et al. (2024b). While the application is novel, the theoretical foundation is heavily borrowed
Convergence assumption in Theorem 4.1 is acknowledged as intractable to verify; empirical validation (Appendix E.1) is helpful but doesn't constitute formal theoretical guarantee

Composability claims are overstated—only one compositional experiment demonstrated (German math→English), and evidence shows negative interference when combining modules with different objectives (e.g., readmission+LOS modules; Appendix J.5)
Mode collapse explanation for GRPO Full's temperature sensitivity is incomplete—may be hyperparameter/dataset specific rather than fundamental; no ablation on β or clipping parameters to verify
Significant practical limitation: tokenizer mismatch severely degrades cross-architecture transfer (Llama→Qwen drops to 18.3 from 35.6 baseline; Appendix D.2), contradicting 'universal' framing
Inference cost increase not negligible—naive UniR increases per-token time by 58% (Table 6), requiring speculative decoding mitigation rather than being inherently efficient
Experimental design concern: UniR uses βKL=0 while GRPO baselines use βKL=0.04; though justified as necessary for reasoning module learning, this makes controlled comparison difficult
Limited analysis of when UniR fails—appendix J.5 shows semantic misinterpretation errors but provides no systematic characterization of problem classes where reasoning modules cannot help
Hyperparameter choices appear somewhat ad-hoc (βKL=0 justified post-hoc citing DAPO paper) and β parameter sensitivity not thoroughly explored despite its theoretical importance
Medical experiments use synthetic MIMIC-IV research data; generalization to real clinical deployment unclear despite appropriate ethical disclaimers
